name: THE CELL BLOCK
rule: VAMILY rules 416 (the big interiors: the tile stays a house), 461, 451(a) (its ceiling at 10%), 59 (every tile its cost and its effect), 428 (roofs and cover), 441; ask row 468's list, the twelfth: 'THE PRISON's cell blocks: smaller, still house-tiled.'
facts: A prison's housing unit is cells in two tiers round a dayroom: the lower cells open onto the dayroom floor, the upper ones onto a walkway with a rail, stairs at its ends; officers watch from a glass control room (the picket).
On house tiles a cell is far smaller than a tile, so a tile of cells is a whole run of cell fronts: a wall you cannot cross, its doors racked open.

When a unit is taken from inside, the first things done are the same everywhere: mattresses dragged out into barricades, the toilets plugged so the floor floods, a fire in the dayroom. The board is a unit after that.
The valley's prisons stand out in the desert; the jail is a tower downtown. This board is the inside of either.
how_to_mod: A layout is 15 strings of 20 characters; every character is in 'legend'; every tile kind a legend entry names has its row in 'tiles' (its cost and its effect). A piece names the finished piece it is drawn as ('like') until this folder has its own art file (prison_art.json: floor lists and a kit, the garage's format). slices/bohemia_big_inside.js lays it; slices/fight_ground/insides.json lists the insides.
districts_why: The prison and the jail are the two map kinds with cell blocks: six fights in ten there are fought inside a unit, by the cell's own dice; the rest in the yard or the street.
tiles_how: Rule 59: every kind of tile says what it costs to step on and what it does. 'row' is the fight's own ground row (flat 2 AP, rough 3, height +1 a level, obstacles none); 'open' is open floor (on AUTO nobody stays on it); 'good' is ground AUTO goes to; 'say' is the one line he reads when he taps it (draft, the fewest words). [bb] each kind is a Battle Brothers ground: flat, rough, a hill, an obstacle, and cover as its trees and walls give it.

wall.effect: The unit's concrete: no way through.

cells.effect: A run of cells, doors racked open, nothing in them worth a fight: no way through.

bars.effect: The sally port's bars between two units: no way through but its gates; you see through them. [bb] its palisade.

floor.effect: The dayroom floor: open ground, and the tier looks down on it; on AUTO nobody stays on it.
floor.say: The dayroom: open ground, and the tier looks down on it.

gate.effect: A sally port gate, its lock cut: open ground, one way through the bars.

table.effect: A steel table and its stools, bolted to the floor: low cover.

barricade.effect: Mattresses dragged out of the cells and stacked into a barricade: cover.

burned.effect: What was burned in the first night, a heap of it: low cover, and slow going over it (3 AP). [bb] its brush.
burned.say: A burned heap: low cover, slow going.

flooded.effect: Where the toilets were plugged and the floor flooded: standing water, open ground, 4 AP a step, and a man standing in it fights worse: a quarter off his melee skill, his melee defence and his ranged defence (COMBAT FOUR 11/20, before this: 3 AP and nothing else). [bb] its swamp: murky water.
flooded.say: Flooded floor: slow going, open ground.

desk.effect: The officers' desk on the floor, turned on its side: cover.

picket.effect: The picket, the glass control room, its glass starred: nobody stands on its tile; cover for the tiles beside it. [bb] its boulder.

fire.effect: A fire somebody keeps in a trash can. It burns day and night: a man in its light is seen.
fire.say_lit: A fire: you stand in its light, and they see you.

doors.effect: The door to the yard, blown: open ground, and by day the light falls in: a man here is seen.
doors.say_lit: The yard door: open ground, and the day is on you.

high.effect: The upper tier's walkway, a storey over the dayroom: high ground. A blow or a shot down from it lands easier, one up at it harder; a gun reaches a tile farther from it. Up the stairs it is a walk; over the rail from the floor it is a climb: no attack that turn, and a beast cannot. [bb] its hill.
high.say: The tier: you hit down easier, and a gun reaches a tile more.

high_mattress.effect: A mattress hung on the tier's rail: low cover, on high ground. They hold the tier at the bell.
high_mattress.say: A mattress on the rail: low cover, and high ground.
high_mattress.say_before: A mattress on the rail: low cover.

ramp.effect: The stairs up to the tier: the WALK up. A step onto them from the floor costs one more; a man who walks up can still strike this turn.
ramp.say_before: The stairs: the walk up, and you can still strike.

kit_how: Every piece is drawn AS a finished piece of another kit ('like') until COOK's own picture for it is in prison_art.json under the same name: then that picture is used and nothing here changes. 'kind' is what it does in the fight (COVER, LOW_COVER, WALL, RAIL, HEIGHT); 'blocks_move' means nobody stands on its tile. A DRESS piece is drawn and never counted.

say.height: The tier: you hit down easier, and a gun reaches a tile more.

gallery.why: THEY HOLD THE TIER: whoever holds the walkway holds the dayroom under it. The band's shooters and its back line, and men enough to make 'least' of the band (never more than 'share'), start up on the tier over their own side; his line starts on the floor: the stairs are his way up.

ceiling.how: VAMILY rule 451(a): the unit's concrete ceiling far up, its caged lights (most dead), the skylight's bars, over the board at this alpha. 'src' is the picture COOK makes; 'have' true the day it is in the folder. Until then the fight draws 'kind' itself, a stand-in (the garage's deck: a concrete slab with its beams and its lights).
